title: BadSampler: Harnessing the Power of Catastrophic Forgetting to Poison Byzantine-robust Federated Learning

problem.claim: Poison Byzantine-robust federated learning by exploiting catastrophic forgetting.

gap.claim: Poisoning attacks against Byzantine-robust federated learning when malicious behaviors are not directly observable remain largely unexplored.

contributions.claim: Formally define generalization error and establish its connection to catastrophic forgetting.
Introduce BadSampler, a clean-label data-poisoning attack that selectively samples high-loss training data to increase model generalization error.
Formulate the attack as an optimization problem and propose Top-κ sampling and meta-sampling as approximate adversarial sampling strategies.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The formal error upper bound and time-complexity analysis indicate that the design preserves attack utility with high efficiency.
Evaluations on two real-world datasets report the effectiveness and performance of the proposed attacks.

narrative_sequence.summary: Federated learning is vulnerable to poisoning attacks through manipulated local data or model updates.
Byzantine-robust aggregation rules can detect and mitigate poisoning effects in observable malicious-behavior settings.
Poisoning scenarios without such directly observable behaviors are underexplored.
The paper connects generalization error to catastrophic forgetting and develops BadSampler with two adversarial sampling strategies.
The paper reports efficiency analysis and evaluations on two real-world datasets.

source_observation.claim: A clean-label adversary can selectively feed high-loss training data to increase generalization error.

interpretation.claim: Data-selection behavior may create a poisoning pathway even when the data labels remain clean.

application.claim: Robust federated-learning defenses should consider adversarial sampling patterns in addition to manipulated labels or updates.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this lesson transfers beyond Byzantine-robust federated learning.

unknowns: The two evaluated datasets are not identified.
Quantitative results, baselines, and experimental settings are not provided.
The adversary capabilities and operational assumptions are not fully specified.
Details of the formal error bound and time-complexity analysis are omitted.
